reps.brief:
YOUR ITEMS (phone evidence in docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/loop6-bugs.json: appBugs 1, 2, 5 and checks apk10-go-to-board-no-empty-frame / apk10-sounds-first-ranked; earlier work in docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/fix-loop4.json, area 'pregame', GoCover.tsx):
1) In 3 of 4 ranked games (motion on), there is still an empty run of about 80 ms (5 frames with only the ambient background) at the switch from the match screen's count GO! to the game route's GO! cover (apps/mobile/src/screens/match/GoCover.tsx, apps/mobile/app/game.tsx). It comes about 0.55 s after GO! first shows. So the route's first frame is not drawn in the same frame the match screen leaves. Find the real gap: the native stack transition (animation 'none'/'fade'?), the match screen unmounting before the new route's first draw, or GoCover's first frame waiting for something. Make the old GO! stay on screen until the new one is drawn: keep the match screen's GO! under the new route, or use an opaque transition with no frame between. Respect Reduced Motion.
2) Empty frames between Results ('משחק חדש') and the search screen: the same kind of handoff gap. Find it and overlap the two screens.
3) The first ui_tap after a cold start ('שחק') and the first cell_select in the first game are still silent (sfx.ts FIRST_PLAY_AT_S warm-up from loop 4 fixed the countdown cues only). Find why the first play of a player that was never played is dropped: an expo-audio player not loaded yet? Preload and warm up the tap/select cues at app start (silently), so the first real play is heard. Add a Jest test with the audio mocks.

items.id: 1 apk10-go-to-board-no-empty-frame (pregame-found-countdown-reduced): empty frames between the count's GO! and the game route's GO! cover
items.rootCause: The gap comes from the stack transition into /game, not from GoCover. GoCover's cover starts at opacity 1 and never fades in, so the 'fades in from 0 over ~80 ms' that QA saw has to be react-native-screens' own 'fade'. The match→game change was a router.replace with the `flow` fade. native-stack's default animationTypeForReplace is 'push', so the new screen fades 0→1 over the fixed 150 ms (rns_fade_in.xml) while the old one fades out. The old screen's content is not reliably there during that fade, because of a race in react-native-screens 4.26.2. Fabric's differ (Differentiator.cpp) emits the Remove mutations for the old Screen's descendants before the Screen's own Remove. RNSScreenRemovalListener sees the removal in pullTransaction, but NativeProxy.notifyScreenRemoved only *posts* `screen.startRemovalTransition()` to the UI thread (`screen.post {}`). When the mount batch runs before that posted runnable, the old screen's views are gone at once. All that is left is the new screen at alpha ≈0 over the wandering digits: 5–7 empty frames, then the rest of the fade. Because it is a race, it showed in 3 of 4 games. Game 4's 'dip only' (YMAX 197 ≈ 0.77) is what a correct cross-fade of two identical frames looks like.
items.fix:
New apps/mobile/src/screens/match/goHandoff.ts:
- The GO! handoff state (handGoCover/handedGoCover) moves here, so the root layout can read it without loading CountdownView at startup. GoCover re-exports both, so the API is unchanged.
- New GO_HANDOFF_TRANSITION = { animation: 'none', animationTypeForReplace: 'push' }.
- New gameRouteTransition(flow): returns the cut when a GO! is handed, and `flow` otherwise.
apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx: /game's options are now `() => gameRouteTransition(moves.flow)`. Navigators evaluate the options function on every render, so the replace commit itself carries stackAnimation 'none' / replaceAnimation 'push' for the game screen. Any other way into /game (practice, a room) keeps the fade.
With 'none', react-native-screens uses rns_no_animation_20 (alpha 1→1). GoCover's first frame (the same still GO!, drawn where the match screen drew it) is fully opaque from its first draw. Whatever the old screen still shows for that frame is the same picture.
GoCover's own GO!→game fade, and its Reduced Motion variant, are unchanged. So is goHoldMs, so GO!→board timing does not change. docs/design/motion.md `go` row: one sentence added.
items.test:
New apps/mobile/src/screens/match/__tests__/goHandoff.test.tsx, 5 tests:
- gameRouteTransition with and without a handed GO!, Reduced Motion off and on.
- On the real expo-router native stack: match → handGoCover → router.replace('/game') gives the game's RNSScreen stackAnimation 'none' and replaceAnimation 'push'. A plain push to /game gives 'fade'.
- The root layout wires /game's options to it.
- The react-native-screens facts it relies on: push-replace uses the new top's animation, NONE is rns_no_animation_20, and NativeProxy posts startRemovalTransition. This flags a library upgrade.
On the old code the suite fails: no goHandoff module, and the layout used `options={moves.flow}`.
Also run: MatchScreen, GoCover, gameRoute, ranked e2e, rankedNewGame e2e, interferenceRanked e2e, transitions and startupGraph. All pass.
items.deviceCheck:
Needs a new APK.
1) Reduced motion off. Run 4 ranked games: 'שחק' → '2 שחקנים' → 'מהיר' → 'מצא יריב' against the hidden bot, with screenrecord. Check every frame from GO!'s first frame to the first board frame. Expected: no frame with only the ambient background, and no frame where GO!, the strip or the ghost board dip toward 0. At the route switch (~0.25 s after GO! is at full size), GO! stays put at full brightness (YMAX stays at GO!'s level). After that, only GoCover's own cross-fade GO!→board (~240 ms) shows.
2) Same with reduced motion on (2 games): no empty frame, no movement at the switch, and GO!→board is a ~200 ms fade.
3) GO! first frame → first board frame should stay about the same as apk10 (~1.3 s, or ~1.0 s with reduced motion).
4) Tap a cell right after the board appears: it responds. Android back during GO! does nothing.

items.id: 2 results-search-gap (pregame-found-countdown-reduced): empty frames between Results 'משחק חדש' and the search
items.rootCause: It is the same race as item 1. 'משחק חדש' called startRankedAndOpen(…, 'replace') (or startAndOpen for a practice). react-native-screens faded the match screen in from 0 over 150 ms while the removed results screen faded out. But the results' views were often already deleted by Fabric before the posted startRemovalTransition ran. So the search (also entering with its own useEnter fade from 0) faded in over an empty screen: 7–8 frames of ambient only.
items.fix:
The next screen is now pushed over the results, never put in their place, so the results stay whole under it for the whole native cross-fade.
- apps/mobile/app/results/[id].tsx: newGame uses 'push' for the practice and ranked targets and resolves true when it pushed. Friends and rooms still replace or dismiss, unchanged.
- The route then calls the new apps/mobile/src/screens/results/dropWhenCovered.ts. It waits until the results are covered: the stack's `transitionEnd` with closing:true, which react-native-screens sends when the covered fragment's exit animation ends, or COVERED_DROP_FALLBACK_MS = 600 at the latest.
- It then removes the results route from the stack with CommonActions.reset, unseen. Back from the search therefore goes where it went before, and the stack never grows.
- It never drops the results while they are the screen shown (back within the fade), and it acts only once.
- The route awaits the drop, so the results' button keeps its spinner while they fade out. They unmount in the drop commit, so no state change rides along.
Reduced Motion: the stack's reduced fades still apply. docs/design/motion.md `flow.fade` row: one sentence added.
items.test:
New apps/mobile/src/screens/results/__tests__/resultsNewGameOverlap.test.tsx, 5 tests:
- On the real native stack, a results stand-in wired like the route: after 'משחק חדש' both RNSScreens are there and the results are still in the tree (a replace removed them at once).
- Firing the results' onDisappear drops them: 2 screens left, and back goes to Home.
- The route source pushes and hands itself to dropWhenCovered. This fails on the old code.
- dropWhenCovered unit tests: drops on a closing transitionEnd, not on an opening one, and only once; the fallback drop comes at 600 ms; it never drops the shown screen.
Updated pins that asserted 'replace':
- resultsRoute.test.tsx (startAndOpen now 'push'; fails on the old code).
- match/__tests__/rankedResults.test.tsx (router.push('/match')).
rankedNewGame.e2e (the full ranked results → 'משחק חדש' → search → game flow) and the other results suites pass.
items.deviceCheck:
Needs a new APK.
1) Reduced motion off. Finish a ranked game, then on Results tap 'משחק חדש' with screenrecord (3 times). Expected: no frame with only the ambient background between the results and 'מחפש יריב…'. The results fade out while the search fades in over them (a normal cross-fade dip at most).
2) After the search is up, Android back (cancel) goes to where it went before this change: the game type screen or Home, NOT the old results. Repeat 'משחק חדש' 3 times in a row, then back out step by step: the stack never shows old results.

items.id: 3 pregame-found-sound / apk10-sounds-first-ranked: first ui_tap after a cold start and first cell_select of the first game are silent
items.rootCause:
The FIRST_PLAY_AT_S = 1 ms first-play seek from loop 4 saves long clips only.
Part 1, measured: ui_tap is 45 ms and cell_select is 60 ms (22050 Hz mono). Every cue that worked is 260–390 ms long.
Part 2, from media3 behaviour (not measured): media3's WAV reader hands the clip to the player in ~100 ms chunks, so a 45–60 ms clip is a single chunk. After a seek to 1 ms, that chunk starts on the sample at or before 1 ms (frame 22, 0.998 ms). The player then drops a chunk that starts before the position it was sent to. So nothing is left to play.
Part 3, matches dumpsys: the seek flushes and releases the old track ('stopped / releasing player'), and no new track ever starts.
What holds on the phone either way: two kinds of play always work.
- A play right after the player is made (the old lazy path).
- Every play after the first: a real seek back from the end. That is why 'מצא יריב' (the second ui_tap) was heard.
The loop-4 code also sent a lazily made player through the 1 ms seek. That had the same risk for short clips.
items.fix:
apps/mobile/src/services/sfx.ts:
- Every player made by preload (Home's warmModes, the game/search warm-up, GameScreen and the levels' preloadCues) plays once at once, at volume 0, while the app is in the foreground. Nobody hears it. A WeakSet `warming` holds these players.
- The first real play restores the sound's volume (volumeOf) and seeks to 0. That makes it a 'second play', heard whole from the start, for short and long clips alike, so long cues no longer lose their first ~100 ms either.
- Muted warm-ups don't count toward MAX_CONCURRENT_SOUNDS, so UI ticks are never dropped because of them.
- A player made lazily inside play() now plays from 0 (the path that always worked) instead of 1 ms.
- FIRST_PLAY_AT_S remains only for a preloaded player left cold (preload while backgrounded).
No timing change to the warm-ups or to GO!→board.
items.test:
New apps/mobile/src/services/__tests__/sfxWarmUp.test.ts, 8 tests. Its expo-audio stand-in follows QA's evidence and the chunk explanation above: an idle preloaded player is 'drained', a seek to the same position while ready is skipped, and the WAV is read in 100 ms chunks, dropping a chunk that starts before the seek position. Each sound file is mocked to its own source, so players are told apart.
It covers:
- Cold start: Home preloads ui_tap, then the first 'שחק' is heard at 0.3 from 0 ms (was not heard).
- The first game's first cellSelect is heard (was not heard).
- The warm-up is never heard, and the volume is restored.
- matchFound, beats and GO are heard from 0 ms (were heard from 100 ms).
- Both count_tick voices are warmed.
- A lazy player is not warmed and is heard.
- Muted warm-ups don't block a tap.
- Background preload does not warm.
7 of the 8 fail on the old sfx.ts (checked by swapping in the refs/qa/snap-loop6 version and restoring it).
Updated to the new behaviour: sfx.test.ts (preload now plays muted), sfxFirstPlay.test.ts (counts heard starts; the first seek is 0 after the warm-up), feedback.test.ts (preloadCues: one muted play each) and warmPressCue.test.tsx.
items.deviceCheck:
Needs a new APK. Media volume up (phone 3 had media volume 0, so check by dumpsys and by ear). Sound on, both phones.
1) Force-stop, launch, wait ~3 s on Home, then 'שחק'. In `adb shell dumpsys audio` (PlaybackActivityMonitor, the app's uid) expect:
- one event:started for ui_tap about 1.2–2 s after Home showed: the muted warm-up, unheard;
- then a new event:started at the 'שחק' tap, heard as a soft click.
2) Continue '2 שחקנים' → 'מהיר' → 'מצא יריב'. During the type screen and the search, a burst of muted starts (the warm-up) is expected. matchFound, the 3 beats and GO are heard whole, with their attack not clipped.
3) In this first game, tap a cell. cell_select is heard and logs event:started at the tap (was 'stopped / releasing' with no start). The first correct digit is heard.
4) A solo practice and a staged level right after a cold start: the first cell tap is heard.
5) Sound off in Settings: nothing is heard anywhere (warm-ups stay muted).

rep.notes:
Checks run:
- npx jest on 143 suites (screens/game, screens/levels, components/levels, src/__tests__): all 2742 tests pass.
- npx jest on 84 suites (screens/match, screens/results, gameRoute, ranked / rankedNewGame / interferenceRanked / solo / bot e2e, startupGraph, theme, services, screens/home): all pass after updating rankedResults.
- npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit: clean.
- eslint: clean on all changed files.
- prettier --write and --check: only on my files.
- No i18n keys added. No adb, APK, deploy, install, stash or commit. The server was not touched.

The root cause for items 1 and 2 is a race in react-native-screens 4.26.2 on Android. NativeProxy.notifyScreenRemoved posts startRemovalTransition (`screen.post {}`) from the mounting thread. Fabric's differ removes the outgoing Screen's descendants before the Screen itself. So whenever the mount batch runs first, a *removed* screen is blank for its whole exit fade.

The same race affects every other replace in the app, for example:
- game → results;
- game-type → practice game;
- bot-select → game;
- match → bot (onBot);
- friends.
QA has not flagged these yet. I fixed only the two reported handoffs, in JS. The proper fix is native: run startRemovalTransition before the mount items, e.g. from a UIManagerListener.willMountItems in RNS, through a patch-package patch (the repo already uses patch-package for Reanimated). That needs a native build and a device check, so I left it for the main session to decide.

After the drop, goHoldMs still subtracts Android's 150 ms native fade (flowFadeMs). That fade no longer runs on match→game, but GO!→board timing is unchanged, because the board's arrival is driven by GoCover's own phases. If QA wants GO! seen a little longer, use the iOS-style subtraction of GoCover's 240 ms. I left MatchScreen untouched.

The results' drop at transitionEnd deletes the results' views (including the spinner's CSS animation) ~150 ms into the search. The old replace deleted them in the very commit that mounted the search, so the B14/B32 Reanimated-retire exposure is no worse than before. Watch logcat for '[Reanimated]' failures at that moment.

The sfx warm-up means each preloaded player logs one extra muted event:started in dumpsys. QA should not count these as heard sounds.

Test-environment note: rendering the real app/results/[id].tsx inside a minimal renderRouter Stack hangs in Jest, on the snapshot code as well (not caused by these changes). So the stack-level overlap test uses a stand-in wired exactly like the route, plus a source pin, and the real route is covered by resultsRoute.test and rankedNewGame.e2e.

reps.brief:
YOUR ITEMS (phone evidence in docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/loop6-bugs.json: appBugs 3, 4 and check apk10-2p-header-360dp; earlier work in docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/fix-loop4.json, area 'game'):
1) 2P game header at 360dp (wm density 540) in ENGLISH: 'No mistakes' breaks mid-word, 'Interfere' shrinks to tiny text (Moshe hates tiny text), and the VS badge covers the opponent's flag. Make the 2P header fit at 320–360 dp in every layout language without mid-word breaks and without shrinking text below design sizes: reflow (secondary info on its own line, shorter labels via existing i18n keys, icon-only for the interfere button with an accessibility label), and keep VS clear of the flag. Test at 320 and 360 dp in en, de, ru, he.
2) In the arsenal (interference picker) the 'יעד' chip on the opponent's frame is half covered by the scrim. The chip must be fully above the scrim (z-order, or place it inside the highlighted frame).

items.rootCause: There were three causes. (1) My mistakes text has numberOfLines=2 with adjustsFontSizeToFit. When a word is wider than its line, Android breaks it in the middle and does not shrink it, because the line count still fits. At 320 dp (density 540 on the A16; card 140) the room beside my two 44-dp buttons is 44 dp, and 'mistakes' needs 58, so it showed 'No mi / stakes'. Even at 159 dp, id 'kesalahan' (66) is wider than the 63-dp room. (2) The 2P 'Interfere' button keeps its word and shrinks it to fit beside the activity. Even on a 159-dp card, only he, ja, zh and pl fit at full size. English drops to about 0.8 at 159 and lower at 140, so the word looks tiny. (3) The cards are only 8–10 dp apart at 320–360 dp, but VS is 36 wide and centred, so it reaches about 13–14 dp into each card's identity row. That row's inner side holds the opponent's flag (and my flag and rating).
items.fix: New components/player/statusFit.tsx: hidden, accessibility-hidden width probes (copies of the words in the same Text and style) report each word's width at full size on the phone. Pure rules decide from those widths. interfereWordFits: the word stays only when 'Interfere' at full size fits beside the activity at full size (max of 'Thinking…' and ring + gap + the lock or paused word). Otherwise InterferenceButton gets iconOnly: the bolt alone in a 44x44 box with flexShrink 0 and the same accessibility label. mistakesWordsFit: the words stay only when every word fits its line and they take at most 2 lines. Otherwise MistakesText gets mark: the 'cancel' icon (16) and the count in Teko 500 22 (the delta's design size), with the same red flash and pop (pop off under Reduced Motion, as before). Until the probes are measured, the card looks as designed. When the count changes, the card keeps its current form while the new words are measured. VS: vsInset(row, card) = ceil((36 − gap)/2 + 4). DuelHud passes it as PlayerCard innerInset, which pads the inner side of the identity row (paddingEnd on mine, paddingStart on the mirrored opponent card; RTL-aware). That is 17 dp at 360, 18 at 320, 2 at 390 and 0 from about 400. Shortened two translations (D124 practice, no new keys): nl activity.paused 'Gepauzeerd' to 'Pauze' and tr 'Duraklatıldı' to 'Durdu'. At 320 dp they were wider than the line beside the icon. Text sizes never go below the design sizes: score 64, name 16, status body 14. components.md §3.1, §3.2, §8.1 updated.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/screens/game/__tests__/DuelHudFit.test.tsx renders DuelHud at 320 and 360 dp in en, de, ru and he, with 0 or 1 mistakes. It fires the probes' layout with the fonts' real advances (widthIn). Mine: the words show only when every word fits the room at full size in at most 2 lines, else mark + count (en and ru at 320 get the mark; de and he keep the words). Opponent: the 'Interfere' word shows only for he at 360. Otherwise the button is icon-only, 44x44, with the same accessibility label, and 'Thinking…' and ring + 'Choosing' fit the rest at full size. VS: each identity row's inner content ends at least 2 dp before VS. It also checks that before measuring the card looks as designed, that at 390 the inset is at most 2, and that in all 19 layout languages, at 320 and 360, the activity words (male and female) fit at full size beside the icon. This fails for nl and tr without the shortened words, and the whole file fails on the old code (no probes, mark, iconOnly or inset). Ran: player components (incl. statusFit, PlayerCard), screens/game (69 suites, 1172 tests), ranked/botPractice e2e, dev sections, i18nParity, i18nCheck, widthBudget, interferenceDocs, localizationDocs: all pass. tsc: the only error is apps/mobile/src/services/__tests__/feedback.test.ts (another agent's file). eslint is clean, prettier was run, and i18n-check shows 0 errors.
items.deviceCheck: Phone 3 (SM-A165F), font size 1.0. A) wm density 540 (320 dp), app in English, ranked 2P (the hidden bot is fine). 1) My card: instead of 'No mistakes' it shows a small boxed-X mark and '0' in the big condensed digits. No word is broken ('No mi / stakes' is gone) and nothing is tiny. 2) Make one mistake: the number becomes '1', briefly red, with a small pop (with Remove animations on: red only, no pop). 3) Opponent card: the interfere button is only the lightning icon in a 44-dp square, with no 'Interfere' word and no tiny text. TalkBack, or the content-desc in a ui dump, reads 'Interfere with <name> · costs N pts'. A tap opens the picker as before. 4) The VS badge sits in the gap between the cards and covers neither flag nor my rating. Names may end in '…' a little sooner. B) Same density in German, Russian, Italian and Hebrew: the button is icon-only in all of them. My mistakes: de 'Keine / Fehler' and he 'אין / טעויות' in two full-size lines, ru as mark + number, it as mark + number. Nothing breaks inside a word. C) Normal density (physical 450): in Hebrew the button reads 'הפרעה' at full size (not shrunk) and 'אין טעויות' is two full-size lines. In English the button is icon-only and 'No / mistakes' is two full-size lines. VS does not touch either flag (it may sit very close at about 2 dp). D) Optional, nl or tr at density 540, under an interference (opponent paused): 'Pauze · A8' / 'Durdu · A8' with no mid-word break. Reset the density afterwards.

items.id: interference-picker-opens ('יעד' chip half under the scrim)
items.rootCause: The scrim's hole is targetFrameOf(card), which is the target frame: 6 + 2 dp around the card. TargetFrame drew the 'יעד' chip (20 dp) with bottom −10 inside the frame's border. So the chip ended 8 dp below the frame's outer edge, outside the hole, and the scrim (drawn above the cards) dimmed its lower part, at every density and language.
items.fix: The frame now reaches further down, with paddingBottom 14 instead of 6 (metrics.targetFrame.paddingBottom = padding 6 + half the chip 10 − outline 2). marginBottom −16 keeps the card in place. The chip stays where it was (its top 4 dp over the card), and its bottom now sits on the outline's outer edge (chipWrap bottom: −outline). arsenalModel.targetFrameOf extends the hole by the same 16 dp below the card, so the whole chip is inside the hole and stays above the scrim. Applies to 2P and 3–4P compact cards (same TargetFrame and the same hole). components.md §3.4 updated.
items.test: PlayerCard.test.tsx, new test 'the יעד chip lies inside its frame…': it reads the rendered frame and chip-wrap styles and checks that the chip's bottom is at or above the frame's outer edge (on the old code it was 8 dp past it), that its top is still 4 dp over the card, and that the frame's negative margins equal padding + border, so the card does not move. arsenalModel.test.ts: targetFrameOf is now {x 8, y 40, w 175, h 184}, and a new test checks that the hole extends past the card exactly as the drawn frame does on each side (16 dp at the bottom). ArsenalOverlay, useArsenal, pickerFits and GameScreenGroup tests pass.
items.deviceCheck: Phone 3, at density 450 and at 540, in Hebrew, English and Italian: in a 2P ranked or friends game, get 2+ points and tap the interfere button on the opponent card. The yellow frame around the opponent card now reaches about 8 dp lower below the card than on its sides. The 'יעד' / 'Target' / 'Bersaglio' chip sits on the frame's bottom line and is entirely bright, with no darker lower half. The rest of the screen is dimmed as before. Close and reopen 3 times: same result. In a 3–4P room, the chip on the targeted compact card is fully bright too.

rep.notes: At wm density 540 the A16 is 320 dp wide (1080/3.375), not 360. Tests cover both 320 and 360. Fitting is measured at runtime by hidden probes (hidden from accessibility, so ui dumps do not show duplicate texts), so it follows the phone's fonts and the system font scale. In ui dumps the opponent's 'Interfere'/'הפרעה' text node is gone wherever the button is icon-only, so QA should find the button by content-desc ('Interfere with …'). Moshe's 17.10 decision (the word 'הפרעה' on the button) still holds wherever it fits at full size: Hebrew on 360 dp and wider. Elsewhere the icon-only fallback is used instead of tiny text; flag this to Moshe in case he prefers another option. Not covered: (a) the turn-based activity variant (D1 'turns', 'Their turn ·') is not measured for the word-vs-icon decision, because that mode is not live; (b) the Italian 'Sconfitt/e' break on the player profile card (apps/mobile/src/screens/player), also mentioned in appBug 3, is a different screen and is untouched; (c) the existing B47 shrink to .75 remains in the code only as a safety net. tsc's only error is in apps/mobile/src/services/__tests__/feedback.test.ts (another agent's file). The temporary width-measuring test I used for planning was deleted. No adb, builds, installs or git write operations were used.

reps.brief: YOUR ITEM (docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/loop6-bugs.json appBug 6, task account-settings-licenses-expand): the licence texts on the licences screen (apps/mobile/src/screens/legal/LicensesScreen.tsx and its data) keep 80-column hard line breaks, so the lines are ragged on a phone. Reflow the text: join the single newlines inside a paragraph into spaces, and keep blank-line paragraph breaks and list or indented lines (numbered clauses, the MIT/OFL headings). Do this at build time in the licence generator, or at render. Keep LTR. Test it with a sample OFL/MIT text.

items.rootCause: The licences screen (Expandable in apps/mobile/src/screens/legal/LicensesScreen.tsx) showed each licence body exactly as stored in third-party-licenses.json. That text is the licence file verbatim, with its 80-column hard line breaks, so each hard break forced a new line on top of the phone's own wrapping. The result was ragged lines of one or two words, e.g. 'person obtaining' / 'a copy of...' and '(the' / '"Software")...'.
items.fix: New pure function reflowLicense(text) in apps/mobile/src/legal/licenses.ts, applied at render time when an Expandable opens. The generated JSON and scripts/licenses.mjs are unchanged, so nothing needs regenerating. It works one blank-line block at a time and joins each paragraph's single newlines with spaces. Blank-line paragraph breaks stay. A line stays on its own line when it is: a rule ('-----'), a markdown heading ('#'), a short all-capitals first line (PREAMBLE, DEFINITIONS, DISCLAIMER...), a list item ('1)', '2.', '(a)', '*', '-', '•'), a copyright notice ('Copyright (c) 2020...' but not 'Copyright Holder(s)' inside a sentence), or a line indented differently from its paragraph (keeps the Apache header's centred lines). A list item continues on a line that sits under its text (hanging indent, Apache '(a)' and BSD '*') or flush with its marker (OFL '1)'). Each paragraph keeps its first line's indent. Every word is kept. The LTR styles are untouched.
items.test: apps/mobile/src/screens/legal/__tests__/LicensesScreen.test.tsx has 4 new tests. (1) A screen test opens a sample MIT text and checks the body's exact children (toHaveProp('children'), because toHaveTextContent folds newlines). It FAILS on the old code (checked by temporarily rendering the raw body: 1 failed) and passes now. (2) reflowLicense on a sample OFL excerpt (rules, headings, a definition containing 'Copyright Holder(s)', clauses 1) and 3), the all-caps DISCLAIMER). issues.problem: Item 1 (GO! to game cut) almost certainly does not reach the device. gameRouteTransition() reads the module-level `handed`, and the navigator re-evaluates the options function on every render. The real /game route clears `handed` in a passive effect (`useEffect(() => handGoCover(null), [])`). It also renders `<Stack.Screen options={{ gestureEnabled: false }} />`, which calls navigation.setOptions in a layout effect, and because the options object is new each render it calls it on every render. That forces a synchronous navigator re-render right after the replace commit. React flushes the pending passive effects first, so `handed` is already null and /game's options flip back to `flow` ('fade') in the same JS task. On Android, RNS reads `newTop.screen.stackAnimation` only in ScreenContainer.performUpdates, which onScreenChanged posts with runOnUiQueueThread after the mount batch. Both commits are mounted by then, so the native transition is still the 150 ms fade from 0: the same symptom. goHandoff.test.tsx misses this because its stand-in game route calls neither handGoCover(null) nor Stack.Screen.
issues.evidence: I ran a scratch Jest test, outside the repo, with the real goHandoff and the same Layout as goHandoff.test. The only change: the game stand-in does what app/game.tsx does (`useEffect(() => handGoCover(null), [])` plus `<Stack.Screen options={{ gestureEnabled: false }} />`). Output: `options evaluations for game: ["none","fade"] handed now null`, and the final RNSScreen has `stackAnimation: 'fade'` (expected 'none'), so the test FAILS. Sources: node_modules/expo-router/build/react-navigation/core/useDescriptors.js getOptions (the function is called on every render; setOptions is navigator state). expo-router build/views/Screen.js (setOptions in useSafeLayoutEffect, deps include `options`). react-native-screens ScreenContainer.kt onScreenChanged → runOnUiQueueThread { performUpdates() }, and ScreenStack.kt line ~204 reads newTop.screen.stackAnimation at that point.
issues.suggestion: Make the cut sticky for the route that took the handoff. Options: (a) key it on the game route instead of the global: in app/game.tsx pass `animation: 'none'` (when goCover != null) inside its own Stack.Screen options, which are per-route overrides and survive later renders; or (b) clear `handed` only when GoCover reaches 'done' or the route unmounts, not on mount. Better still, use item 2's pattern here as well: push /game over the match screen (cut or fade) and drop the match screen with dropWhenCovered. The old GO! then really stays under the new one (see the next issue). Change the goHandoff test's game stand-in to mirror app/game.tsx (handGoCover(null) in an effect plus Stack.Screen setOptions), or render the real route.

issues.problem: Even with 'none' held, the cut may still leave one empty frame. By the agent's own root cause, Fabric deletes the old screen's descendant views in the mount batch. RNS attaches the incoming Screen (fragment transaction in onUpdate) only in the runnable posted by onScreenChanged/runOnUiQueueThread, which runs after the current Choreographer doFrame. That doFrame draws a traversal with the match screen emptied and the game screen not yet attached. 'none' removes the 150 ms fade-in from 0, but not this frame. The brief asked to keep the match screen's GO! under the new route until the new one is drawn, and a replace cannot guarantee that.
issues.evidence: react-native-screens 4.26.2: ScreenContainer.kt onScreenChanged comment ('We schedule the update to run after the current Fabric commit has finished'), with runOnUiQueueThread { performUpdates() }. ScreenStack attaches new screens only through the fragment transaction in onUpdate. The fix's own test pins NativeProxy's posted `screen.post { screen.startRemovalTransition() }`, which is the same posting pattern. No device evidence either way: the deviceCheck has not been run.
issues.suggestion: Use the push-then-drop approach from item 2 for match→game. The match screen and its GO! stay fully mounted under /game, and GoCover's first frame then draws over them. Drop the match route once covered. Device-check frame by frame as the report describes.

issues.problem: dropWhenCovered's drop() has try/finally with no catch. If navigation.getState() or dispatch throws, for example after the results route's navigator went away or on a stale state reset, the exception escapes from the setTimeout or event-listener callback. In a release build an uncaught JS error in a timer is fatal.
issues.evidence: apps/mobile/src/screens/results/dropWhenCovered.ts: `try { const state = navigation.getState(); ... navigation.dispatch({...CommonActions.reset(...)}) } finally { resolve(); }`. The function is called from both `setTimeout(drop, fallbackMs)` and the transitionEnd listener.
issues.suggestion: Add a catch that reports through crashReporter / console.warn and continues. The drop is best-effort.

issues.problem: Sound item 3: a player that is preloaded while the app is in the background is neither warmed nor marked played, so its first play still seeks to FIRST_PLAY_AT_S (1 ms). By the report's own explanation, that silences 45–60 ms clips (ui_tap, cell_select). Example: Home's warmModes or GameScreen preloadCues firing just as the app is backgrounded. The first tap or cell select after returning is then silent again.
issues.evidence: sfx.ts voices(): `if (!warm) {...played.add} else if (inForeground()) { created.forEach(warmUp) }`. A warm preload in the background leaves the player cold, and play() then uses `played.has(player) ? 0 : FIRST_PLAY_AT_S`. The report states 'FIRST_PLAY_AT_S remains only for a preloaded player left cold (preload while backgrounded)'.
issues.suggestion: Warm cold players on the next foreground transition (the AppState subscription already exists), or have the first play of a cold player recreate it lazily (the path that is known to work) instead of seeking to 1 ms.

issues.problem: reflowLicense keeps each paragraph's leading indent. In Apache-2.0, every definition paragraph starts with 6 spaces and the header lines with 23–27 spaces ('                           Version 2.0, January 2004'). On a ~40-character phone line, those become a large first-line indent, or a line that wraps into leading whitespace. The rest of the paragraph runs to the margin, so Apache still looks uneven, though no longer broken mid-sentence. OFL, MIT, ISC, BSD and BlueOak reflow cleanly.

items.id: 1 apk10-go-to-board-no-empty-frame (pregame-found-countdown-reduced): empty frames between the count's GO! and the game route's GO! cover
items.rootCause:
The gap comes from the stack transition into /game, not from GoCover. GoCover's cover is opaque from its first frame. The match screen *replaced* itself with /game using the `flow` fade. On Android, react-native-screens 4.26.2 then fades the new screen in from 0 over 150 ms while the old one fades out, but the old screen's content is not reliably there: NativeProxy.notifyScreenRemoved only posts `screen.startRemovalTransition()` to the UI thread. Fabric's differ removes the old Screen's descendants in the mount batch, so when that batch runs first, the match screen is blank at once. That is a race, which is why it showed in 3 of 4 games.
The reviewer found two problems in my first fix, and both are confirmed.
(a) The 'none' cut was not sticky. app/game.tsx clears the handed GO! in a passive effect, and its `<Stack.Screen options>` calls setOptions on every render. That re-renders the navigator in the same JS task, so /game's options function flipped back to 'fade' before RNS read stackAnimation in its posted performUpdates. I reproduced this: with the real game route's behaviour, the old code ends on 'fade'.
(b) Even a held 'none' cannot keep the old GO! under the new one during a replace: the match screen's views are deleted in the mount batch, while the new fragment is only attached in a posted runnable.
items.fix:
1) apps/mobile/app/match/index.tsx: onPlay now runs `router.push('/game')` (it was replace). It then calls `dropWhenCovered(navigation, routeKey)`, the same helper as item 2. The match screen and its GO! stay fully mounted under /game. RNS keeps the old fragment drawn until the new one is attached, and with 'none' (rns_no_animation_20) both are on screen together for ~20 ms. The match route leaves the history unseen once it is covered: on its closing transitionEnd, or after 600 ms at the latest. Back from the game therefore goes where it went before.
2) apps/mobile/src/screens/match/goHandoff.ts: gameRouteTransition(flow, routeKey) now decides per route key, once, the first time the navigator evaluates that route. It stores the decision in a Map that keeps the last 8 keys. A /game route that came in over a handed GO! keeps 'none' / animationTypeForReplace 'push' for as long as it exists, whatever the effects or setOptions do later. Every other way into /game (practice, a room) keeps the fade.
3) apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx: /game's options are now `({ route }) => gameRouteTransition(moves.flow, route.key)`.
GoCover's own GO!→board fade (240 ms; 200 ms with Reduced Motion) and goHoldMs are unchanged, so GO!→board timing is the same. The docs/design/motion.md `go` row now describes the push-then-drop.

items.id: 2 results-search-gap (pregame-found-countdown-reduced): empty frames between Results 'משחק חדש' and the search
items.rootCause: It is the same race as item 1. 'משחק חדש' replaced the results with the search (or a practice game). RNS faded the new screen in from 0 over 150 ms, but Fabric often deleted the results' views before the posted startRemovalTransition ran. apps/mobile/app/results/[id].tsx: newGame pushes the practice or ranked target over the results ('push') and resolves true. The route then awaits dropWhenCovered(navigation, routeKey) (apps/mobile/src/screens/results/dropWhenCovered.ts). The helper removes the results from the stack with CommonActions.reset once they are covered: on the stack's closing transitionEnd, or after COVERED_DROP_FALLBACK_MS = 600 at the latest. It never drops the screen being shown, and it acts only once. Friends and rooms keep replace or dismiss.
This round, per review: drop() now has a catch that reports through crashReporter().recordError(error, 'dropWhenCovered'), and the addListener call is guarded too, with the fallback timer still dropping. A throwing navigator can no longer escape from a timer or native-event callback. The helper is now also used by the match route (item 1).

items.id: 3 pregame-found-sound / apk10-sounds-first-ranked: first ui_tap after a cold start and first cell_select of the first game are silent
items.rootCause:
Loop 4's first-play seek to 1 ms (FIRST_PLAY_AT_S) saves long clips only.
Measured: ui_tap is 45 ms and cell_select is 60 ms (22050 Hz mono); every cue that was heard is 260–390 ms long.
From media3's behaviour (not measured on the phone): the WAV reader hands over ~100 ms chunks, so a 45–60 ms clip is a single chunk. After the 1 ms seek, that chunk starts at 0.998 ms, before the seek position, and is dropped. dumpsys matches this: the old track is released and no new start follows.
On the phone, two kinds of play always work: a play right after the player is made (the lazy path), and every second play (a seek back from the end).
Reviewer's low issue, confirmed: a player preloaded while the app was in the background was neither warmed nor marked as played, so its first play still went through the 1 ms seek and stayed silent for short clips.
items.fix:
apps/mobile/src/services/sfx.ts:
- Every player made by preload in the foreground plays once at once at volume 0 (the warm-up). The first real play restores volumeOf(id) and seeks to 0, so it is a 'second play', heard whole from the start, for long cues too. Muted warm-ups don't count toward MAX_CONCURRENT_SOUNDS.
- NEW this round: a player left cold, because it was preloaded in the background, is warmed by the next preload in the foreground (Home's warmModes, the game and search warm-ups, GameScreen's preloadCues). If a real play comes first, play() removes the cold player and makes a fresh one on the spot (the lazy path), so it is heard whole.
- FIRST_PLAY_AT_S and the 1 ms seek are removed: every play now seeks to 0. Header and comments updated.
items.test:
apps/mobile/src/services/__tests__/sfxWarmUp.test.ts, now 9 tests. The expo-audio stand-in models an idle 'drained' player, a skipped same-position seek, and 100 ms WAV chunks that drop a chunk starting before the seek point.
- Cold start: the first 'שחק' is heard at 0.3 from 0 ms.
- The first cellSelect of the first game is heard.
- The warm-up is never heard, and the volume is restored.
- matchFound, beats and GO are heard from 0 ms.
- Both count_tick voices are heard.
- A lazy player is not warmed.
- Muted warm-ups don't block a tap.
- NEW: after a background preload, the first ui_tap, cell_select and correct are each heard from 0 ms, the cold ui_tap player is removed, and no extra players pile up. (Old code: ui_tap and cell_select silent; correct from 100 ms.)
- NEW: a player made in the background is warmed by the next foreground preload, only once, and its first real play is heard. (Old code: never warmed, silent.)
Also passing: sfx.test.ts, sfxFirstPlay.test.ts, feedback.test.ts and warmPressCue.test.tsx.

rework.notes:
How each review issue was handled:
- HIGH (non-sticky cut): confirmed and fixed. The cut is decided once per /game route key, and the scratch-test scenario is now the repo test: the game stand-in mirrors app/game.tsx.
- MEDIUM (a replace can't keep the old GO! under the new one): fixed by the suggested push-then-drop. app/match/index.tsx pushes /game and drops itself with dropWhenCovered.
- LOW (dropWhenCovered with no catch): fixed. Errors in dispatch, getState or addListener go to crashReporter().recordError, and the fallback still drops.
- LOW (a cold player preloaded in the background): fixed. The next foreground preload warms it, and a play that comes first remakes it lazily. FIRST_PLAY_AT_S is removed.

Checks run:
- npx jest on 82 suites (screens/match, screens/results, screens/home, services, theme, gameRoute, ranked / rankedNewGame / interferenceRanked e2e, startupGraph, a11yAudit): 1470/1470 pass.
- friendsDocs and levelsSpecDocs: pass.
- npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit: clean.
- eslint on all changed code files: clean.
- prettier: --write on my files, and motion.md checks clean from the repo root.
- No i18n keys added, server not touched.
- No adb, APK, deploy, install, stash or commit.

Things for the main session to watch:
(1) Between the push and the drop (≤600 ms, usually ~20 ms after the 'none' cut), the match screen stays mounted under the game. Its tick re-renders and BackHandler stay alive for that moment: the game's handler is registered later and wins, and MatchScreen's `left` ref blocks a second onPlay or onLeave.
(2) goHoldMs still subtracts Android's 150 ms flowFadeMs, which no longer runs on match→game. GO!→board timing is unchanged because GoCover drives it. MatchScreen is untouched.
(3) The same replace race still affects other replaces QA has not flagged: game → results, game-type → practice, bot-select → game, match → bot (onBot), friends. The proper fix is native: run startRemovalTransition before the mount items, e.g. a patch-package patch to RNS. That needs a native build and a device check.
(4) Each warmed player logs one extra muted event:started in dumpsys. QA should not count these as heard sounds.
